plotSections.title: Qualin's Quax apothecary
bullets: Walker and Plymouth enter Qualin's Quax, a Sunder apothecary run by a stately duck-like Aarakocra in blue and purple robes.
Plymouth asks for dragon gizzard; the shopkeeper Quaylin says stock is low and sells it by the pound.
Walker fails a perception check with disadvantage from exhaustion and becomes fixated on Quaylin’s heirloom gem rather than the negotiation.
Plymouth secures dragon gizzard at five gold per pound while Walker misses part of the exchange.

plotSections.title: The Quackless and Walker's distraction
bullets: Quaylin wears a family-heirloom purple gem called the Quackless of the Quinn’s line.
It is not for sale; Quaylin ballparks its value at about five million gold for a lord like Walker.
Walker is mesmerized by the gem and admits he came in for exhaustion relief, not jewelry.

plotSections.title: Potions of vitality
bullets: Quaylin produces a milk-crate holder for five vials with one slot empty and four potions of vitality remaining.
The potions look like greater healing potions but in a lighter fuchsia shade.
Each potion removes all exhaustion from a long day of adventuring, cures poison and similar ailments such as snake bites or basilisk effects, and improves healing on the next short rest.
Quaylin sells them for twelve hundred gold apiece and offers the Quax guarantee: if it quacks or cracks, Walker can bring it back for a refund.
Walker is too worn down to haggle and cannot afford twelve hundred gold right now.

plotSections.title: Dragon hoard financing
bullets: Quaylin suggests Walker use the Haven Hold dragon hoard for liquid cash instead of paying out of pocket.
The dragon can loan gold at very low interest, with conversion around a couple silver per gold, and may simply give gold away if he likes a customer.
Walker does not want to run another Sunder Chase circuit, but Quaylin clarifies he can talk to the dragon directly for a loan without racing.
Walker decides to go speak with the dragon and leaves the shop after shaking Quaylin’s feathered hand.

plotSections.title: Walker's gold hand
bullets: Quaylin notices Walker’s gold-colored hand and taps it with a pestle, confirming it is real flesh rather than metal for sale.
Walker begins explaining it came from swimming in cold molten-looking water, possibly during time at the Temple of I in the north.
Plymouth silently signals Walker to stop talking about the hand.
Quaylin asks whether loon folk were involved; Walker says no, and Quaylin expresses hatred for loon folk.

chronologicalEvents: Walker and Plymouth enter Qualin's Quax and meet Quaylin, a duck-like Aarakocra shopkeeper.
Plymouth asks for dragon gizzard; Quaylin says it is sold by the pound.
Walker rolls perception with disadvantage and becomes distracted by the shop and Quaylin’s gem.
Plymouth buys dragon gizzard at five gold per pound.
Walker learns the Quackless of the Quinn’s line is worth about five million gold and not for sale.
Walker asks Quaylin for help with constant exhaustion.
Quaylin shows four remaining potions of vitality in a five-vial crate.
Quaylin prices each potion of vitality at twelve hundred gold with the Quax guarantee.
Walker says he cannot afford that much and is too tired to haggle.
Quaylin tells Walker to seek a loan from the Haven Hold dragon hoard.
Walker refuses a Sunder Chase run but agrees to talk to the dragon directly.
Walker shakes Quaylin’s hand and heads out to find the dragon.
Quaylin taps Walker’s gold hand with a pestle and asks what alchemical event caused it.
Walker starts to explain an incident involving cold molten-looking water and possibly the Temple of I.
Plymouth gestures for Walker to stop discussing the gold hand.
